title: Characters and the terminating null
goal: Distinguish string length, array capacity and the position of the terminating null.

prerequisites.text: Be able to index an array and separate input validation from the calculation.

terms.title: Null terminator
terms.definition: A byte with value zero. It marks the end of a C string and is written as '\0'.

terms.title: String length
terms.definition: The number of bytes before the first null terminator.

terms.title: Array capacity
terms.definition: The number of bytes the whole char array can hold.

sections.title: How much space a label needs
paragraphs: A stockroom label reads OK and has five cells available. Reading stops at the first cell that holds zero. The remaining cells still belong to the buffer, and the label length is two.
A C string is a sequence of bytes ending at the first '\0'. The character '0' is visible in text such as T09. The terminating '\0' marks the boundary.
A label with n single-byte text characters needs at least n + 1 cells. For these labels, strlen gives the number of visible characters.

sections.title: Where reading stops
paragraphs: Mark the indices of O, K and the terminating '\0' before running the program. The actual output appears below the listing.
steps: The cells array contains five bytes.
Printing with %s and measuring with strlen both stop at cells[2].
Both operations use the first two bytes, producing OK 2.
trace: Beyond the end of the string

sections.title: Who establishes the boundary
paragraphs: First establish that a '\0' lies inside the array. C supplies it automatically for a string literal. When filling separate cells, the program sets its position.
Measuring a sequence without this guarantee can read beyond the array. Trace this case by index on paper.
The separate diagnostic passes two arguments to strlen. Clang rejects the call. Use sizeof separately to measure the array capacity.

sections.title: Lay out a new label
paragraphs: Draw the cells of label S007. Identify the first null index, string length and minimum capacity before writing code.

selfcheck.prompt: What does strlen return for the array in the example?
feedback: The array capacity is 5. The first null determines the string length.
O and K are before the first '\0'.
The third byte marks the end and contributes zero to the length.

selfcheck.prompt: What fills label[3] for the label T09?
feedback: '0' adds a visible digit to the text.
This byte terminates the string after three characters.

selfcheck.prompt: What must you establish before using strlen on an array you filled by hand?
selfcheck.feedback: Name an index or condition that guarantees a '\0' inside the array. For T09 that is cell 3 of an array with capacity 4.

practice.title: Make a numbered label
practice.task: Read the tens digit and the ones digit from separate lines. Accept values from 0 to 9. Print the letter T, then the digits in that order and the length after a space. Print invalid for an invalid number, a value out of range or a missing line. The supplied read_integer checks the numbers. The task considers the first two lines.
practice.hint: Compare the assignments to label[1] and label[2]. Use distinct digits and keep label[3] for '\0'.
criteria: Inputs 0 and 9 give T09 3. Inputs 9 and 9 give T99 3.
The array holds three text bytes and the terminating '\0' at position 3.
An incorrect digit or missing line gives invalid.
Cases marked “automatic WASI check” use exact bytes. Read their labels and expected output. You can enter the other cases in the lesson editor.
